title: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ)
summary: MQTT v3.1.1 and v5 connect handshakes with the CONNACK checked, plus reconnect-storm ramps. Includes an enterprise test plan (jobs starting ent-).
description: Load tests an MQTT broker (Mosquitto, EMQX, HiveMQ, VerneMQ): MQTT 3.1.1 and 5 connect handshakes with the CONNACK checked, a TCP accept-only test and a reconnect-storm ramp. It models thousands of devices reconnecting at once after an outage.

variables.name: host
variables.guide: The host name or IP address of the server, without a port or http://, for example redis.staging.example.com. BLASTA runs in a container, so for a service on your own machine use host.docker.internal instead of localhost.

variables.name: port
variables.description: MQTT port (1883; 8883 is TLS and is not supported here)
variables.guide: The port the service listens on. The default is filled in; check the service's configuration if you changed it.

jobs.name: CONNECT v3.1.1
jobs.notes: A real MQTT CONNECT (clean session) with the 'connection accepted' CONNACK checked: the cost of every device reconnect. Every request uses the same client id, so a broker that enforces unique ids will drop the previous connection: that is the session-takeover path, and it is expected.

jobs.name: CONNECT v5
jobs.notes: MQTT 5 CONNECT with empty properties. Only the CONNACK packet type is checked: a v5 CONNACK carries a variable-length property list, so its reason code cannot be matched byte for byte. A broker without v5 support closes the connection or answers with another packet, counted as a failure.

jobs.name: reconnect storm ramp
jobs.notes: Ramps connections per second to find the accept ceiling: the fleet-reconnect after a broker restart or network blip.

jobs.name: TCP accept only
jobs.notes: Connection accept with no MQTT traffic: kernel and listener backlog.

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 01 smoke
jobs.notes: Enterprise plan, step 1 of 10. One request a second for 30 seconds. Run this first, every time: it proves the address, credentials and headers are right and that the environment is up before any real load is applied. Gate: zero errors. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 01 smoke

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 02 baseline (20% load)
jobs.notes: Step 2 of 10. About a fifth of normal traffic for 5 minutes: the uncontended latency of this request. Every later result is judged against it, so record p50 and p95. Gate: at most 0.5% errors and the default latency targets. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 02 baseline (20% load)

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 03 average load (SLO check)
jobs.notes: Step 3 of 10. Normal busy-hour traffic for 10 minutes. The rate is the reference job's rate: raise it to your measured production peak-hour rate. This is the run that proves (or breaks) your SLO. Gate: at most 1% errors, p95 and p99 inside the targets. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 03 average load (SLO check)

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 04 peak load (2x average)
jobs.notes: Step 4 of 10. Twice the average for 10 minutes: the busiest hour of the year plus headroom. Latency may rise, but must stay in SLO; if it does not, you have no headroom. Gate: at most 2% errors, latency targets doubled. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 04 peak load (2x average)

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 05 stress (ramp to 4x)
jobs.notes: Step 5 of 10. Ramps to four times average over 10 minutes, then holds for 2. Finds where it degrades and HOW: gracefully (latency rises, errors stay low) or badly (errors, timeouts, crashes, restarts). Observation only, no gate. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 05 stress (ramp to 4x)

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 06 spike (10x in 10 s)
jobs.notes: Step 6 of 10. Reaches ten times average within 10 seconds and holds for 2 minutes: a campaign email, a news link, a failover. Checks autoscaling, queue limits and load shedding. Gate: at most 5% errors, because shedding load is acceptable and crashing is not. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 06 spike (10x in 10 s)

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 07 recovery after the spike
jobs.notes: Step 7 of 10. Run IMMEDIATELY after the spike, at average load for 5 minutes. Latency and errors must return to the baseline from step 2. If they do not, something is stuck: queues, connection pools, GC, an autoscaler cool-down. Gate: same as average load. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 07 recovery after the spike

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 08 soak (1 hour at 60%)
jobs.notes: Step 8 of 10. One hour of steady load. Finds leaks and slow decay in memory, connections, file descriptors, disk, log volume and cache churn. Watch the resource graphs: any line that climbs and never flattens is a finding. Gate: at most 0.5% errors. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 08 soak (1 hour at 60%)

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 09 breakpoint (find the ceiling)
jobs.notes: Step 9 of 10. Ramps to twenty times average over 20 minutes. Stop it when errors pass about 5%: the rate at that moment is your ceiling, and ceiling divided by peak is your capacity margin. Use a production-like environment, never production. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 09 breakpoint (find the ceiling)

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 10 resilience window (failover / deploy)
jobs.notes: Step 10 of 10. Average load for 15 minutes. About 5 minutes in, cause the event you are testing: kill a pod or node, fail over the database, roll out a new version, drain a zone. Errors in the window are your real availability loss. Gate: at most 1% errors overall; read the time series for how long the dip lasted. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): 10 resilience window (failover / deploy)

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): connection storm (ramp to 10x)
jobs.notes: Ramps new connections per second to ten times normal: a fleet reconnecting after an outage, a deploy that restarts every pod, a network blip. Shows accept-queue, file descriptor and handshake limits. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): connection storm (ramp to 10x)

jobs.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): device fleet reconnect storm
jobs.notes: Thousands of devices reconnect after an outage, all at once. Ramps to twenty times normal over 3 minutes. Reference request: CONNECT v3.1.1.

job.name: MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX / HiveMQ / VerneMQ): device fleet reconnect storm
